- **Incremental Backups:**  
  Are you making regular, automated backups of your archive? Even a simple scheduled export (daily/weekly) to a separate location (Dropbox, external drive, etc.) can be a lifesaver.

- **Conflict Resolution & Manual Sync:**  
  Some platforms let you review sync conflicts or manually trigger syncs. If possible, get in the habit of syncing before and after major editing sessions, and check for any unsynced changes before closing the app.

- **Annotation Export:**  
  If annotations are especially valuable, is there a way to export them separately or keep a running log (even a simple text file or email to yourself) as you work?

- **Atomic Saves:**  
  Some advanced tools (like git-based note systems) save every change as a new version, so you can always roll back. Would you be open to using a system like this, or is that overkill for your needs?

- **Offline-First Editing:**  
  If sync failures are common, consider working offline and only syncing when you have a stable connection.

- **Third-Party Sync Monitors:**  
  There are tools that can watch a folder or database and alert you if files change or fail to sync, providing an extra layer of oversight.
